extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners (primary) and patent applicants / practitioners (secondary)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for determining when a reference qualifies as prior art under AIA 35 U.S.C. 102 (including 102(a)(1), 102(a)(2)) and for applying the statutory exceptions in 35 U.S.C. 102(b), plus procedural mechanisms to overcome 102 rejections and required form paragraphs for Office actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: 102(a)(1) prior art qualification (printed publication, public use, sale, other availability)
rubrics_metrics.description: A reference qualifies as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) if the reference predates the effective filing date of the claim; the sale or use of the invention need not occur in the United States to qualify.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2152. Examiner should consider whether the reference predates the effective filing date. Practical note: worldwide sales/uses/availability can qualify as prior art. (Rev. 10.2019)

rubrics_metrics.name: 102(b)(1)(A) grace period inventor disclosure exception
rubrics_metrics.description: A disclosure which would otherwise qualify as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) is not prior art if: (1) it was made one year or less before the effective filing date of the claimed invention; and (2) it was made by the inventor or a joint inventor, or by another who obtained the subject matter directly or indirectly from the inventor or joint inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §§ 2153.01(a) and related discussion. Office personnel will not apply a disclosure as prior art if it is apparent from the disclosure itself that it is by the inventor or joint inventor (e.g., names the inventor as author and does not name additional authors). If not apparent, applicant may submit evidence (e.g., affidavit/declaration). Applicants may identify grace period disclosures in the specification per 37 CFR 1.77(b)(6) to expedite examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: 102(b)(1)(B) grace period inventor-originated public disclosure exception
rubrics_metrics.description: A disclosure which would otherwise qualify as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) may be excepted as prior art if: (1) the disclosure was made one year or less before the effective filing date of the claimed invention; and (2) the subject matter disclosed had been previously publicly disclosed by the inventor, a joint inventor, or another who obtained the subject matter directly or indirectly from the inventor or joint inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §§ 2153.02 and 717.01(b)(2). Affidavits/declarations under 37 CFR 1.130(b) may be used to show prior public disclosure by the inventor (MPEP § 2155).

rubrics_metrics.name: 102(a)(2) prior art qualification (U.S. patents, U.S. patent application publications, WIPO publications)
rubrics_metrics.description: U.S. patents, U.S. patent application publications published under 35 U.S.C. 122(b), and PCT (WIPO) published international applications are prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) if the filing or effective filing date of the disclosure of the reference is before the effective filing date of the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if issue/publication date is not before the effective filing date, the reference may still be applicable under 102(a)(2) if it was 'effectively filed' earlier for the subject matter relied upon. See MPEP § 2152.01 (effective filing date) and 35 U.S.C. 102(d) / MPEP § 2154 for rules on when subject matter was effectively filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: 102(b)(2) exceptions to 102(a)(2) (A),(B),(C)
rubrics_metrics.description: Three exception provisions limit the use of U.S. patents/published applications/WIPO publications as prior art under 102(a)(2): (A) exceptions when another obtained the subject matter from the inventor/joint inventor; (B) exceptions when the subject matter was effectively filed by another after prior public disclosure by the inventor or originator; (C) exceptions when the disclosed subject matter and the claimed invention were owned by the same person or subject to an obligation of assignment to the same person (or were subject to a joint research agreement) not later than the effective filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(A)-(C) and MPEP §§ 2154 and 717.02. 102(b)(2)(C) concerns common ownership/JRA and can avoid certain prior art; it resembles pre-AIA 103(c) but with important differences (see MPEP § 2154.02(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanisms to overcome a 102(a)(1) or 102(a)(2) rejection — benefit claim under 35 U.S.C. 120
rubrics_metrics.description: Overcome a rejection by submitting a benefit claim under 35 U.S.C. 120 within the time period set in 37 CFR 1.78 by providing the required reference to a prior application in a corrected application data sheet under 37 CFR 1.76 and by establishing that the prior application satisfies the enablement and written description requirements of 35 U.S.C. 112(a), or filing a grantable petition to accept an unintentionally delayed benefit claim under 37 CFR 1.78.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 211 et seq. This requires showing the earlier application satisfies 112(a) (enablement and written description).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanisms to overcome a 102(a)(1) or 102(a)(2) rejection — benefit claim under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) (provisional)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit a benefit claim under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) within the time period set in 37 CFR 1.78 by providing the required reference to a prior provisional application in a corrected ADS under 37 CFR 1.76 and by establishing that the prior provisional satisfies the enablement and written description requirements of 35 U.S.C. 112(a), or file a grantable petition to accept an unintentionally delayed benefit claim under 37 CFR 1.78.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 211 et seq. Establishing 112(a) support in the provisional is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanisms to overcome a 102(a)(1) or 102(a)(2) rejection — foreign priority under 35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit a claim to priority under 35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d) within the time period set in 37 CFR 1.55 by identifying a prior foreign application in a corrected ADS under 37 CFR 1.76 and by establishing that the prior foreign application satisfies the enablement and written description requirements of 35 U.S.C. 112(a), or file a grantable petition to accept a delayed priority claim under 37 CFR 1.55.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The foreign priority filing date must antedate the reference and be perfected; perfected filing requires filing a certified priority document (and English translation if necessary) per 37 CFR 1.55(g). See MPEP §§ 213 - 216.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanisms to overcome a 102(a)(1) or 102(a)(2) rejection — affidavits/declarations under 37 CFR 1.130
rubrics_metrics.description: File an affidavit or declaration under 37 CFR 1.130 to establish that an applied reference or disclosure that was not made more than one year before the effective filing date of the claimed invention is not prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a) due to an exception listed in 35 U.S.C. 102(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under 1.130(a), an affidavit/declaration of attribution may be submitted to disqualify a disclosure as prior art because it was made by the inventor/joint inventor or obtained from them. Under 1.130(b), an affidavit/declaration of prior public disclosure may be submitted to disqualify an intervening disclosure if the subject matter had been publicly disclosed by the inventor/joint inventor (see MPEP §§ 717 and 2155).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanisms to overcome a 102(a)(2) rejection — establishing common ownership or a Joint Research Agreement (102(b)(2)(C))
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish common ownership or provide evidence of a Joint Research Agreement to overcome a 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) rejection (or a 35 U.S.C. 103 rejection based on 102(a)(2)) by establishing entitlement to the 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C) exception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §§ 717.02 and 2154.02(c). Evidence must establish that the disclosed subject matter and the claimed invention were owned by, or subject to assignment to, the same person (or were subject to a JRA) not later than the effective filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.06 — Notice re prior art available under both pre-AIA and AIA
rubrics_metrics.description: Use ¶7.06 when a prior art rejection is made in an application with an actual filing date on or after March 16, 2013, that claims priority to or the benefit of an application filed before March 16, 2013; this paragraph notifies that correction of statutory basis will not be a new ground if rationale and prior art are same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: This form paragraph must be used in all Office Actions when applicable; it should only be used ONCE in an Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.07.aia — Statement of Statutory Basis, 35 U.S.C. 102
rubrics_metrics.description: Quotation of the appropriate paragraphs of 35 U.S.C. 102 forming the basis for rejections under this section; used in first actions on the merits and final rejections (statute need not be re-cited in all actions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: Use only once in a given Office action; required in first actions on merits and final rejections. For applications claiming priority to pre-March 16, 2013, must be preceded by 7.06. If statute not cited, use form paragraph 7.103 instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.08.aia — 102(a)(1) Activity Before Effective Filing Date
rubrics_metrics.description: (a)(1) the claimed invention was patented, described in a printed publication, or in public use, on sale, or otherwise available to the public before the effective filing date of the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This paragraph should only be used for applications filed on or after March 16, 2013 and must be preceded by form paragraphs 7.03.aia and 7.07.aia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.12.aia — 102(a)(2) reference naming another inventor with earlier effective filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: (a)(2) the claimed invention was described in a patent or application publication in which the patent or application names another inventor and was effectively filed before the effective filing date of the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by form paragraph 7.07.aia and used only in applications filed on or after March 16, 2013 where claims are examined under AIA 102/103.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.15.aia — Rejection 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1)/102(a)(2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim(s) [1] is/are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102 [2] as being [3] by [4].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Notes: Use only for applications filed on or after March 16, 2013 under AIA 102/103; must be preceded by 7.03.aia and 7.07.aia (may be preceded by 7.08.aia). Use only for specified reference types (U.S. patent under 151, U.S. patent application publication under 122(b), or WIPO publication with earlier effective filing date). Include explanation if using 'anticipated' vs 'clearly anticipated'. For priority-claiming applications filed before March 16, 2013 must be preceded by 7.06.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.15.01.aia — Provisional rejection 102(a)(2) (copending application with common assignee/applicant/joint inventor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim(s) [1] is/are provisionally rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) as being anticipated by copending Application No. [2] which has a common [3] with the instant application. Based upon the earlier effective filing date of the copending application, it would constitute prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) if published or patented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provisional rejection may be overcome by: (1) showing under 37 CFR 1.130(a) that subject matter was obtained from the inventor/joint inventor (102(b)(2)(A)); (2) showing under 37 CFR 1.130(b) of a prior public disclosure (102(b)(2)(B)); or (3) a statement under 102(b)(2)(C) establishing common ownership or JRA. This rejection may not be overcome by filing a terminal disclaimer (In re Bartfeld). Use only for AIA-examined apps filed on/after March 16, 2013 and must be preceded by 7.03.aia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.15.02.aia — Rejection 102(a)(2) with common assignee/applicant/joint inventor(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim(s) [1] is/are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) as being [2] by [3]. The applied reference has a common [4] with the instant application and, based on earlier effectively filed date, constitutes prior art under 102(a)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rejection might be overcome by (1) 37 CFR 1.130(a) showing the reference was obtained from the inventor/joint inventor (102(b)(2)(A)); (2) 1.130(b) showing of prior public disclosure (102(b)(2)(B)) if same invention isn't being claimed; or (3) 102(b)(2)(C) statement of common ownership/JRA. Must be preceded by 7.12.aia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.16.aia — Rejection 102(a)(1) based on public use/on sale/other public availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) based upon a public use or sale or other public availability of the invention. [2]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This paragraph must be preceded by 7.03.aia and a full explanation of the evidence establishing public use/sale/availability must be provided in bracket 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.17.aia — 102(a)(1) rejection using prior art excepted under 102(b)(2)(C)
rubrics_metrics.description: Used to reject a claim over a U.S. patent, U.S. patent application publication or WIPO publication with an earlier effective filing date that has been excepted as prior art under 102(b)(2)(C) but is still applicable as prior art under 102(a)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may rely on 102(b)(1)(A) (1.130(a)) or 102(b)(1)(B) (1.130(b)) to overcome the 102(a)(1) rejection. Must be preceded by 7.03.aia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.18.aia — Rejection pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(g)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(g) as being [2] by [3]. (Addresses priority of invention and interference-type determinations.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only for applications/patents examined under AIA 102/103 that contain or contained a claim to an invention having an effective filing date before March 16, 2013 or a specific reference under 35 U.S.C. 120/121/365(c) to such a claim. Must be preceded by 7.14.aia or 7.103.

rubrics_metrics.name: When a disclosure is 'apparent' as a grace period inventor disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Office personnel will not apply a disclosure as prior art under AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) if the disclosure: (1) was made one year or less before the effective filing date of the claimed invention; (2) names the inventor or a joint inventor as an author or an inventor; and (3) does not name additional persons as authors on a printed publication or joint inventors on a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the publication names additional authors beyond the application’s listed inventors, it may not be apparent and will be treated as prior art unless applicant provides evidence. Example: if application names A and B as joint inventors and the publication names A, B and C as authors, the publication would be treated as prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant identification of grace period inventor disclosures in the specification (37 CFR 1.77(b)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants can include a statement designating any grace period inventor disclosures in the specification per 37 CFR 1.77(b)(6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not required, but identifying prior disclosures may expedite examination and save costs. If the specification contains a specific reference to a grace period inventor disclosure and it doesn't name additional authors/joint inventors, the Office will consider it apparent that the disclosure is by the inventor/joint inventor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of affidavit/declaration under 37 CFR 1.130 when disclosure is not apparent
rubrics_metrics.description: In situations where it is not apparent from the prior disclosure or the patent application specification that the prior disclosure is by the inventor or a joint inventor, the applicant may establish by an affidavit or declaration under 37 CFR 1.130 that a grace period disclosure is not prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 717 and § 2155.01 for procedures and when to use 1.130(a) (attribution) or 1.130(b) (prior public disclosure). Office has provided mechanisms for filing such affidavits/declarations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of references that can give rise to 102(a)(2) prior art and cross-applicability to 102(a)(1)
rubrics_metrics.description: 102(a)(2) may be applied if the reference names another inventor and is: (a) a U.S. patent under 35 U.S.C. 151 with an earlier effectively filed date; (b) a U.S. patent application publication under 35 U.S.C. 122(b) with an earlier effectively filed date; or (c) a WIPO publication of an international application or design application that designates the U.S. with an earlier effectively filed date. If any of these types was published before the effective filing date, it is also applicable under 102(a)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See examiner notes in form paragraphs and MPEP § 2152. If a copending application has an earlier effective filing date, it may be used as provisional prior art under 102(a)(2) based on presumption of future publication or patenting.
